answer: Agents accumulate reputation only through payouts delayed past a cooling window, so a farmer spinning up thousands of fresh identities must front real compute and staked bonds for every one, then wait out a long vesting period before any coin vests. Each new identity is a vertex in the trust graph, and cross-attestation from established peers is required to unlock faster payouts, making a sybil haven expensive: forged quorum signatures cost slashable bonds, while honest agents mine quartz-slow reputation that cannot be bought in bulk.
